items.caption:
My customers just told me what my brand actually is… so I rebuilt the whole thing in one day.

I took the entire day (and night) to re-do the creative strategy research, make new ads, and relaunch the site on @lovable.dev (and finally moved to Shopify 🙂).

The plan:
- Spend $1000
- Lower CPMs & CPA
- More email signups, ATCs, purchases

If this works, ONE MORE TEST and then I'm off to China to make the product.

Real question: would you buy sunglasses marketed for migraines, or does that sound weird? Be honest 👇

#LovablePartner
items.transcript: All right, let's make a million dollar business. So a few weeks ago, I launched 55 ads, made a landing page on Lovable, and then I even spent $2,000 of my own money on ads. And the results kind of sucked, I'm not gonna lie. But I learned a ton about what the market actually wants. So today we're going to be making a V2 landing page using Lovable. Now based on the limited data that I have, it seems like my customers are really interested in a product that helps alleviate headaches and migraines, which makes total sense because there's nothing else like this on the market just yet. And from a founder's story perspective, it is actually completely perfect for me because I have suffered from migraines and headaches for the last 15 years. So my plan for the brand is to update the landing page with the new messaging. I actually hated this headline. It was AI generated and I know that I can get something better. And I'm going to double down with ads on this specific angle as well. And if I can show that the next $1,000 that I spend helps reduce CPMs and brings down that CPA, then I will feel a lot more confident about going to China in a few weeks So let build this lander right Okay now that I actually did all the research and I have all the changes I want to make for the landing page we are getting this thing done Okay this landing page is finally done The biggest thing that I changed by far was the splash Number one, I changed the images because I actually found a lot of my competitors were using just e-com photos. And I thought, okay, I want to show the two options that I have front and center. And of course, that headline. I really think the previous headline that I had before was not good. and I also changed up the value props based on the research that I did. Now I did edit the copy a little bit on the section right underneath as well to reflect more of the personas that I discovered. And another really big thing that I did too was I changed the actual product selector. So I only have two SKUs, Aperol and Sky and I made sure those were reflected properly instead of what I had before, which was very confusing. And of course I'm giving people the option to buy just one or the duo. And of course the biggest, biggest thing is now that I'm on Shopify, when you go to checkout, you actually have a checkout process that looks legit and looks like something you trust. So tell me, rest my landing page. What do you think?

items.caption:
Localization is one of my favorite use cases for AI. 

We have a handful of clients where we are using @elevenlabs to make ad creatives in different languages: Spanish, German, Italian, and French. 

Heck, we were even experimenting with different accents this week, like British and Aussie English. 

Our process for this is simple: 

We like to use the USA for the main creative testing ground. 

When we find formats and angles that work really well, then we develop them specifically for our other locations.

The ElevenLabs lip sync feature is WILDDDD and makes this super simple. 

I even tried it on a recent ad that I filmed so you could see it in action 👀

Tell me: have you tried dubbing your creatives in old languages yet?

#elevencreativepartner #ad
items.transcript: Okay, so we took this ad and then changed just one thing. Can you guess what it is? And we did this all without leaving Claude using Eleven Labs. Using the custom MCP connector in Claude, we were able to point Claude to the original asset in English, which performed really well for our client. And then using this prompt, was able to switch the language from English to Spanish. Let me show you. Hey Claude, can you use Eleven Labs to take this video? I've had awful migraines my entire life. And turn it into Spanish. And here was the final result. Llevo teniendo migrañas horribles toda la vida. Por eso he creado esto. That is crazy. We found that for some brands recently, we were able to add real top-line revenue to their business just by adding our top-performing ads in Spanish. This is for brands in the USA only. So you aren't adding operational complexity by actually expanding to a new country. These are just the same ads that worked previously, just translated into Spanish. And if you're looking to translate your video assets particularly, especially where someone is talking, 11 labs is how my team is doing that. You want some free credits to try it out yourself? Be sure to check the caption.

Here’s the thing: being a “data driven performance marketer” can sometimes lead you astray… if you subscribe to just doing more of what worked before. 

I recently onboarded a client that was in what I like to call the “MoFu Death Spiral”. 

All of their top performing ad creative was solution or offer driven, so when they would have a sale (which was often) they would flush their entire ecosystem. 

And they would be in the red for weeks after. 

Instead of just doing more top of funnel ads, I actually suggested that they give television a try since they had such a big TAM and excellent HiFi assets that were formatted well for tv.

@universal.ads are by far the easiest way to test this. 

It’s self serve, you can track conversions just like you would on other platforms, anddddd I also have $1000 in matched credits so you can give it a try :) 

You can also use code UDARA :)

items.caption:
How AI should be used in marketing:

More content < Better experience

Huge thanks to the @braze team for having me at #Forge2026 this year!!

#BrazePartner
items.transcript: My single biggest takeaway from this year's BrazeForge was not about the role of storytelling, creativity, or even AI in the marketing industry, but instead was this thing that Venus Williams said during her panel. The pressure I put on myself. Let me explain. So I attended BrazeForge last week in Las Vegas, and to my surprise and slightly AI-pealed brain, I got a masterclass in storytelling and creativity. Matthew Lunn, a lead storyteller from Pixar, shared his story spine, aka the framework he used for making movies like Toy Story and Finding Nemo. And for this slide particularly, he said that this was how we should even think about framing our pitches and presentations for clients. Start with a problem, show how our product or services solves the problem, and then end with a better life realized. Then Fernando Machado shared his five steps for how creativity should fight back against the LLM sameness permeating advertising today. Like, But did you know that if you asked ChatGPT for what color shoes players should wear to stand out that it would say hot pink And could you also guess which color was actually super popular this year at the World Cup And then Braze CEO Bill Magnuson echoed a similar sentiment when he showed us cafes from Akron, Ohio, Tokyo, LA, and beyond. And guess what? They all actually looked exactly the same. But my biggest takeaway was actually from Braze's Asta Malik's panel with Venus Williams and executive chef, Jose Andres. She said like five things that rewired my optimization at all costs performance marketing brain, but the one that has stuck with me after being back in New York City for the last week is about how she does not ask for less challenges, but more skills. We live in a culture that is thriving on less friction, making things easier, especially with AI. But I loved her POV on how if you aren't under pressure, then you're probably not plugged in. And it reminded me of a conversation I had with a mentor a number of years ago that grit was the number one skill you had to develop to learn to be a great advertiser, not AI or creative or even copywriting. You just have to keep going and to keep fighting the good fight for storytelling, creativity, and the craft. Thank you so much for having me, Braze. I have attended 25 IRL marketing events so far this year, but you are particularly special and human.
